true_answer: Conversely, speakers of Arabic, Farsi, Urdu, and Hebrew read from right to le, and their MTLs unfold leward (past on the right with future on the le); evidence suggests these speakers organize time events in their minds like this as well.[123] ere is also evidence that some cultures use an allocentric spatialization, oen based on environmental features.[122] A study of the indigenous Yupno people of Papua New Guinea found that they may use an allocentric MTL, in which time ﬂows uphill; when speaking of the past, individuals gestured downhill, where the river of the valley ﬂowed into the ocean.
